hypothesis.action: add a required, explicit decomposition record to the discover->frame boundary (one problem or several, and how big is each), gating frame on multi-problem briefs
hypothesis.users: operators running the Nexus lifecycle on non-trivial, multi-faceted work units
hypothesis.outcome: multi-problem briefs are split into independently-routed sub-problems at intake instead of after N failed reviews; a fused brief can no longer silently become a fused frame
hypothesis.evidence: idea-brief Sources 1-6 + RFC Hole 2: one brief fused Problems A/B/C and took six review passes to separate; the failure mode is the decomposition question never being asked, not operators being unable to answer it

success_criteria: A frame run on a single-problem brief records decomposition.problems with exactly one entry and proceeds (test asserts present + length===1).
A frame run on a multi-problem brief returns not_ready and enumerates each sub-problem (test feeds a 2-problem brief, asserts decision==='not_ready' + listed sub-problems).
The decomposition field is required and explicit: a brief with an absent/empty decomposition record does not reach ready.
bun run scripts/test/unit.ts exits 0 with 0 fail markers; bun run typecheck:check shows baseline 0, 0 new.
non_goals: The lane taxonomy itself (RFC item #2) - size_hint is free-text; the typed lane binding lands with #2.
Backward transitions (#3), the spike lane (#4), and Hole 5 / operator-is-worker (owned by Problem A).
Auto-decomposition - the step forces the operator to answer 'one or several?', it does not split problems for them.
Changing /discover's content contract beyond carrying the decomposition record.
out_of_scope: Changing how /plan consumes a single-problem frame.
Per-sub-problem worktrees or routing automation - each sub-problem is framed through the normal path.
acceptance_criteria: Given a discover brief that names two independent problems, when the operator runs /frame, then the frame returns not_ready, lists both sub-problems, and does not emit a single fused design-intent.json.
Given a single-problem brief, when /frame runs, then decomposition.problems has one explicit entry and the frame proceeds to ready.
Given a brief with no decomposition record, when /frame runs, then it does not reach ready (the field is required, not defaulted silently).
open_questions_to_plan: Where the check lives: a typed field on the discover-exit artifact, a gate at frame-entry, or both (the gate is what gives it teeth).
Whether the decomposition record requires a lane per sub-problem now (depends on RFC item #2) or defers lane to free-text size_hint so decomposition ships independently first.
Gate behavior on a multi-problem brief: hard not_ready with enumerated sub-problems, vs route-and-continue (frame the first, queue the rest).

provenance.review_gate: bounded lane: merged review+qa; the frame-stage regression tests are the QA
